svg.title: Anatomy of a black hole, to scale
svg.desc: Animated, to-scale diagram of a non-rotating (Schwarzschild) black hole in units of the Schwarzschild radius r_s = 2GM/c²: event horizon at 1 r_s, photon sphere at 1.5 r_s with photons circling it, innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) at 3 r_s with a hot blob orbiting it. Circular-orbit angular speed in coordinate time is Ω = √(GM/r³) (exact for Schwarzschild), so photons lap (3/1.5)^1.5 = 2.83× faster than the blob. Two light rays are integrated numerically from the photon orbit equation u'' + u = (3/2) r_s u²: impact parameter b = 3 r_s is deflected by 98° (the weak-field formula 4GM/(c²b) = 2r_s/b would give 38°), and b = 2.35 r_s, below the critical b = (3√3/2) r_s = 2.598 r_s, is captured. r_s of one solar mass = 2.953 km; Sagittarius A* (4.297 × 10⁶ M☉, GRAVITY Collaboration 2022, as in site/assets/js/black-hole.js) → 1.269 × 10¹⁰ m = 12.7 million km ≈ 0.085 AU. Source: docs/EQUATIONS.md §5.4.
svg.text: r_s = 2GM/c². Inside, every path leads in.
Light can orbit here, 2.8× faster than the ISCO.
Innermost stable circular orbit: gas inside it plunges.
any ray aimed inside this line falls in
Sagittarius A* (4.3 million Suns): 12.7 million km
